themes.label: Non-parametric methodology & return notation
themes.need: A researcher starting an empirical study of asset returns needs to understand the paper's non-parametric/semi-parametric methodological stance and the price/return/time-scale notation used throughout the survey.

themes.label: Stylized facts: definition and full list
themes.need: A practitioner wants a concise, citable list of the stylized statistical facts (heavy tails, volatility clustering, absence of autocorrelation, etc.) that any candidate return model must reproduce, and how this differs from an event-based explanation of price moves.

themes.label: Statistical estimation pitfalls
themes.need: Someone about to run statistical inference on a financial return series needs to verify the stationarity, ergodicity, and finite-sample assumptions required for their estimators and confidence intervals to be valid.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 1 caption (trash, 87-88) interrupts the continuous discussion of estimator finite-sample validity (ergodicity, estimator-vs-moment distinction, Avogadro-number sample-size analogy, hypothesis-testing/CLT validity); both spans serve one cumulative validity-checklist need.

themes.label: Heavy-tailed unconditional distribution & parametric fits
themes.need: A modeler wants to know how heavy-tailed the unconditional distribution of returns actually is (kurtosis values across assets) and what parametric families are flexible enough to fit it.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 2 and Table 1 captions (trash, 102-103 and 124-125) interrupt the continuous kurtosis-values-to-fit-requirements argument; all three spans serve one need.

themes.label: Estimating tail index via sample-moment method
themes.need: A researcher wants to determine whether the theoretical variance/higher moments of a return series are finite, using Mandelbrot's sample-moment-vs-sample-size diagnostic method.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 3 and Figure 4 captions (trash, 135-136 and 146-147) interrupt the continuous discussion of Mandelbrot's sample-moment method and its erratic higher-moment behavior; all spans serve one need.

themes.label: EVT for tail risk / VaR
themes.need: A risk manager needs to estimate Value-at-Risk or extreme-loss probabilities for a portfolio using extreme value theory (Fisher-Tippett / block-maxima method) applied to asset returns.
themes.distributed_justification: Table 2 caption (trash, 221-222) interrupts the continuous EVT estimation narrative (Fisher-Tippett theorem through empirical tail-index findings); both spans serve one need.

themes.label: Absence of linear autocorrelation in returns
themes.need: A trader or econometrician wants to know whether asset returns show significant linear autocorrelation at various time scales, and why this supports (or complicates) the efficient market hypothesis.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 6/7 caption (trash, 240-241) interrupts the continuous discussion of autocorrelation absence, its definition, and its persistence at longer time scales; both spans serve one need.

themes.label: Volatility-clustering measures via power-transform ACF
themes.need: A researcher wants to quantify volatility clustering in a return series by measuring how autocorrelations of absolute/squared/powered returns decay, and which power is most predictable.

themes.label: Leverage effect & return-volatility decomposition
themes.need: A modeler wants to characterize the leverage effect (negative correlation between returns and subsequent volatility) and needs the return = volatility x noise decomposition underlying GARCH/stochastic-volatility models.

themes.label: ACF reliability limits for heavy-tailed series
themes.need: An econometrician wants to know whether standard ACF-based tests and confidence intervals remain valid when applied to heavy-tailed, nonlinear return series, including squared returns used in GARCH fitting.

themes.label: Cross-asset covariance/correlation & random-matrix theory
themes.need: A portfolio manager building a multi-asset risk model needs to understand how the covariance/correlation matrix of returns behaves and how much of it is genuine signal versus random-matrix noise.

themes.label: Correlations of extreme co-movements
themes.need: A risk manager needs to measure joint tail dependence between assets (probability of simultaneous extreme losses), which the linear covariance matrix cannot capture.

themes.label: Holder regularity & singularity-spectrum definitions
themes.need: A researcher wants the formal mathematical definition of path roughness (Holder exponents) and the singularity spectrum used to characterize the local regularity of a price trajectory.

themes.label: Multifractal formalism: estimating the spectrum
themes.need: A researcher wants to know how to empirically estimate the singularity spectrum of a price series from sample moments via the multifractal formalism and Legendre transform.

themes.label: Empirical spectrum shape & finite-sample artefacts
themes.need: A researcher wants to know the empirically observed shape of asset-price singularity spectra and how much of that finding might be a finite-sample estimation artefact.

unassigned.reason: Pure recap of the paper's preceding sections ('In the preceding sections we have tried to present...'); restates properties already covered across many themes rather than resolving one specific need.

Forward-looking list of open research questions touching several different themes (volatility forecasting, risk management, trading strategy, portfolio risk) at once; recap-shaped preview, not a specific answerable need.
